messages:
pagerduty: ALERT: High error-rate + autoscaler churn detected on hosted-api. Paging oncall. service=redwood-hosted-api severity=high
priya: acked, i'm oncall. jumping in. any customer-facing errors reported?
sam: seeing repeated pod CrashLoopBackOff on runtime-gpu-1 pool. kubectl logs show repeated CUDA OOM + cublas errors.
sam: snippet:
```
2026-03-15T10:22:03Z runtime-gpu-1 pod/serve-xyz Container crashed with error: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
stack: allocate_tensor -> stream_sync -> cublasGemm
```
leo: autoscaler event stream shows rapid scale up then immediate scale down within ~2m window for this pool. scale events: +8 nodes -> -7 nodes -> +6 nodes. that's the thrash.
erin: we have a scale-snapback loop. autoscaler reacting to short-lived spikes causing eviction/reattach thrash. that plus model mem pressure = crashloops.
maya: CS report: 18 customers reported 5xx / high latency starting ~10:20. one enterprise reported failed diffs in testing env.
priya: impact estimate? percent of traffic failing?
customer-support: from logs ~22% of requests to hosted-api model-serving path returned 502/503 during window 10:20-10:30 UTC.
infra-bot: ALERT: node kernel OOM killer invoked on gpu-node-42 at 10:23:01. dmesg: "Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (python) score 987".
sam: root cause hypothesis: autoscaler aggressively scaling because of queued requests; new nodes spin up with warmup delays, pods land, large model cold-start uses peak memory -> OOM -> pod restarts -> autoscaler sees failures and keeps oscillating.
leo: rolling mitigation plan:
- temporarily disable scale-to-zero and burst-scaling for runtime pools
- set cluster-autoscaler --scale-down-delay to 10m
- pin pod resource requests to reduce overcommit
- fallback: route traffic to smaller model variant (model-v2-8bit) while we stabilize
priya: executing now: disabling burst via infra console.
priya: kubectl patch cm autoscaler-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"burstEnabled":"false","scaleDownDelay":"10m"}}'
deploy-bot: Canary rollout for model-v3 paused due to detected instability. rollback recommended.
sam: starting safe-rollout: instruct routing to fallback bucket for 30% traffic -> model-v2-8bit. command: `rdctl routing set fallback hosted-api model-v2-8bit --weight 0.3`
erin: i'm taking 2nd-oncall. handoff @priya -> @erin. priya remaining as incident commander for mitigation steps.
priya: noted. erin, debug note: check kube-scheduler logs for pods stuck Pending due to GPU label mismatch; also check image pull latencies. Also validate driver versions; seen mismatches cause CUDA init failures.
erin: checking driver matrix now, pulling `nvidia-smi` output from node pool:
```
Node gpu-node-17: NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12 Driver 525.85.12
Node gpu-node-42: NVIDIA-SMI 522.78.13 Driver 522.78.13
```
erin: mismatch present. older nodes 522.78.13 likely causing compatibility issues with the runtime image expecting 525.x. scheduling also likely flipped pods onto older nodes during churn.
leo: immediate mitigation: cordon the older nodes to stop new pods: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-42 gpu-node-43` and drain safely for evicted pods.
priya: executed cordon + drain commands. starting reschedule to healthy nodes, but autoscaler still spinning up replacements.
sam: also increasing pod memory limit temporarily to avoid OOM during cold start: patching deployment to higher limits for warmup window.
maya: CS update: telling customers we're investigating, suggested workaround: retry for 30s, we're rolling a fallback model. status page updated.
customer-support: pushed status update: "Degraded: API errors and higher latencies affecting text-generation path. Mitigations in progress."
infra-bot: NOTE: cluster-autoscaler events suppressed while burst disabled. scale down timer extended to 10m.
sam: after cordon + fallback routing, error rate dropped to ~6% in last 5m, pod restarts reduced significantly.
priya: next steps: coordinate with infra to upgrade driver on older nodes to 525.x and set nodeSelector to prefer upgraded pool during rollout. schedule postmortem and update autoscaler heuristics to avoid reaction to short spike-loads.
erin: agreed. creating postmortem ticket and assigning to eng-runtime + eng-sre. incident commander handing back to oncall rotation, leaving mitigation active. will keep watch for 30m.
priya: incident status -> mitigated (customers experiencing reduced errors). follow-ups: driver upgrade, autoscaler config tweak, add guardrail test to prevent scale thrash.
priya: thanks all. :tada:
